candidate.title: TIF-Seq
candidate.scope: The TIF-Seq (Transcript Isoform Sequencing) row of the assigned Illumina poster, at the resolution of its oligo-capping/full-length-cDNA/junction-capture schematic. A single unbranched preparation of capped, polyadenylated RNA is depicted. The 2013 yeast TIF-Seq paper identifies the original implementation; the 2014 protocol clarifies shared transformations and readout without asserting identical complete implementations. The card and row identify one target; the neighboring 2P-seq, 3′-Seq and PEAT rows and right-hand chemical structures are outside its scope. Unshown control branches and adaptations in the papers do not add target workflows.

operations.label: Tobacco acid pyrophosphatase (TAP) treatment
operations.description: Removes the cap from the depicted capped RNA, leaving a ligatable 5′ phosphate while retaining the poly(A) tail.
operations.mechanism: TAP decapping exposes the 5′ phosphate. The primary implementation first dephosphorylates uncapped RNA; this prerequisite is unshown here and is not a separate depicted operation.
operations.information_effect: The RNA end formerly occupied by the cap becomes the attachment site for a known sequence. TAP treatment alone does not establish exclusive selection of previously capped molecules.

b00008, RNA oligo-capping
evidence.quote: The oligo-capping method consists of the selective ligation of an oligo of known sequence to the previously capped RNA molecules. As a first step, total RNA is dephosphorylated to remove any existing 5′ phosphates (e.g., RNA degradation intermediates). After this step, a treatment with Tobacco Acid Pyrophosphatase (TAP) removes the 5′ cap structure and exposes the 5′ phosphate group necessary for subsequent single-stranded RNA ligation.

operations.label: Ligate ‘5oligocap’ oligonucleotide

operations.mechanism: Single-stranded RNA ligation; the primary implementation uses T4 RNA ligase 1.
operations.information_effect: Marks the original capped 5′ boundary and supplies a common handle for subsequent full-length cDNA amplification.

operations.label: Circularize and fragment
operations.description: Joins the ends of the full-length cDNA intramolecularly, then fragments the circles; the circle icon illustrates the intermediate within this combined caption.
operations.mechanism: The primary implementation uses NotI-generated cohesive ends for intramolecular ligation, then sonication. These clarify the combined transformation without expanding unshown substeps.
operations.information_effect: Intramolecular ligation physically juxtaposes cDNA corresponding to the two ends of the same RNA molecule; fragmentation yields junction-spanning fragments together with other fragments. Intermolecular ligation can create misleading end pairings, so affinity enrichment alone does not guarantee single-molecule origin.

evidence.locator: b00010, intramolecular versus intermolecular ligation
evidence.quote: As true intramolecular ligations would result in either A-A or B-B barcode combinations, the combinations A-B or B-A in the final products can only arise due to intermolecular ligations.
evidence.rationale: The primary protocol controls for chimeras with terminal barcodes; these controls are not depicted as a branch in the assigned schematic. Biotin is an affinity handle, not a test of intramolecular origin.

operations.label: Purify
operations.description: Captures biotin-bearing junction fragments on streptavidin beads, enriching them from the fragmented circular cDNA. The poster represents the purified DNA as a short linear cDNA duplex; the capture interface is clarified by the primary paper.
operations.mechanism: Streptavidin affinity binding to the introduced biotin; this changes the selected DNA’s attachment state. The primary protocol retains bead-bound DNA for subsequent library construction, which is unshown here.
operations.information_effect: Retains junction fragments carrying the associated original RNA boundaries. Paper-supported paired-end sequencing identifies co-occurring starts and ends, distinguishing overlapping or differently bounded isoforms; it does not determine internal splicing that leaves those boundaries unchanged. Biotin capture alone does not establish that every junction arose intramolecularly. Full-length cDNA processing favors shorter transcripts. The poster ends at purified cDNA; final adapter construction and sequencing are unshown.

evidence.locator: heading
evidence.quote: TIF-Seq: Transcript Isoform Sequencing

To capture S. cerevisiae transcript isoforms, capped and polyadenylated RNAs were converted into full-length cDNA molecules that were subjected to intramolecular ligation, fragmentation, and capture of the 5′-3′ junctions via a biotin tag (Fig. 1a, Supplementary Fig. S1 and Table S1-S2).

The oligo-capping method consists of the selective ligation of an oligo of known sequence to the previously capped RNA molecules. As a first step, total RNA is dephosphorylated to remove any existing 5′ phosphates (e.g., RNA degradation intermediates). After this step, a treatment with Tobacco Acid Pyrophosphatase (TAP) removes the 5′ cap structure and exposes the 5′ phosphate group necessary for subsequent single-stranded RNA ligation.

evidence.locator: b00329, Figure 1 caption, Detailed experimental workflow of TIF-Seq
evidence.quote: The protocol is composed of: (a) 5′RNA oligo-capping using a DNA/RNA oligo of known sequence (5RNAGsuI), (b) generation and PCR amplification of full-length cDNA, (c) intramolecular circularization after NotI digestion, and (d) purification of paired-end cDNA tags followed by generation of Illumina-compatible sequencing libraries.
evidence.rationale: Full-text evidence for the shared architecture; the different oligo name in this later protocol is not substituted for the poster’s 5oligocap label.
